entities.summary: Marcus Gavius Apicius was a Roman gourmet and lover of luxury who lived during the reign of Tiberius (14-37 CE), leaving behind a culinary legacy that shaped the Roman Empire's gastronomic culture. The Roman cookbook Apicius, often attributed to him, is a testament to his influence on Roman cuisine. Apicius' love of luxury and excess was also the subject of On the Luxury of Apicius, a work by the Greek grammarian Apion, which remains lost to history. Apicius' cognomen, "Gavius," may have been inspired by an earlier Apicius who lived around 90 BC. This enigmatic figure's impact on Roman society and cuisine continues to fascinate historians and food enthusiasts alike.
